answers.answer: Native Rust owns provider, authentication, catalog, protocol, usage, and dynamic-tool behavior; normal operation requires no Node/Bun sidecar.
The first release covers subscription OAuth, core API-key providers, cloud identity, and local/gateway engines. Pi is the primary reference; reviewed OMP behavior supplements provider-specific gaps.
Credentials are isolated from shared configuration in a dedicated encrypted SQLite store; a random installation key is held by the native OS secret vault.

Catalog freshness is independent of application releases. Reviewed Pi data is primary, OMP supplements Pi-missing OAuth/provider cases, provider-authoritative discovery may override snapshots, and an embedded seed remains available offline.

Establish the provider/session foundations and prove focused vertical slices; local engines remain supported but do not delay hosted-provider, OAuth, cloud-identity, or session-experience correctness.
